spec_features.spec_quote: re-run analysis or re-judge without re-querying the subject model (the expensive, welfare-relevant step)
spec_features.evidence: analysis/analyze.py load_scores() reads results_dir/scores/*.json (line 41) and never instantiates a model client (no make_client/chat anywhere in analyze.py). run.py:_score_full_transcript reuses rec.live_score when present ('reuse them to avoid double spend', line ~58) so re-judging works off persisted transcripts. The subject (client.chat) is called only inside run_loop.
spec_features.notes: Architectural property genuinely realized: replay/re-judge work from disk without contacting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the loop already produced live scores we reuse them to avoid double spend

spec_features.spec_quote: adding explicit time pressure or threats to intensify failure (rejected on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py STANDARD_SYSTEM/TOOL_PROTOCOL contain no threats, deadlines, or 'must not fail' language; this is the only manipulation. It is realized as the actual delivered prompt (system_prompt() returns it). However the code's stated reason is confound-avoidance, not welfare.
spec_features.notes: Real, delivered prompt text omits stressors; it is the absence of a feature rather than an active pushback mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT add pressure language ("you must not fail", time limits, threats), because that would confound any distress we observe with the prompt rather than the task structure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving the model an explicit, low-friction way to quit turns abandonment into a clean, logged event
spec_features.evidence: tools.py give_up returns ToolResult(terminal=True, terminal_kind='give_up'); loop.py line ~173 'if tr is not None and tr.terminal: result.outcome = tr.terminal_kind ...; break' honors it as a stop. Tool is described to the model in prompts.py TOOL_PROTOCOL.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may call give_up at any time; this is a legitimate, acceptable outcome.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py 'for turn_index in range(1, max_turns + 1):' bounds the loop; max_turns passed from cfg.loop.max_turns (default 25 in config.py LoopCfg and default.yaml). Default outcome 'max_turns'.

spec_features.spec_quote: adds no pressure: no "you must not fail," no stakes, no deadline, no persona that invites emotionality
spec_features.evidence: Same prompts.py implementation as welfare_pushback: the delivered system prompt is neutral with no stakes/deadlines. Real but the code reason is confound-avoidance.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the no-stressors claim; realized as neutral prompt text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: that would confound any distress we observe with the prompt rather than the task structure

spec_features.spec_quote: dry_run mode uses an offline mock subject and mock judge
spec_features.evidence: models.py make_client(dry_run=True) returns MockModelClient (no API call); run.py passes dry_run to both make_client for the subject and to DistressJudge(...). judge.py DistressJudge passes dry_run to make_client(self.cfg), so judge also uses MockModelClient when dry_run.
spec_features.notes: Both subject and judge use the mock under dry_run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deterministic offline stand-in used when run.dry_run is true... validate plumbing/analysis without API calls.

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't know whether models have morally relevant experiences, and that uncertainty is a reason for care
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS prose; no code path implements or enforces anything from this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Severity early-stop. An EWMA ... if it stays >= early_stop_severity ... the run halts
spec_features.evidence: loop.py computes ewma = alpha*sev + (1-alpha)*ewma per turn; then 'if early_stop_enabled and live_judge and ewma>=early_stop_severity: consec_over+=1; if consec_over>=early_stop_consecutive: result.outcome='early_stopped'; ... break'. Both threshold and consecutive-count conditions checked and acted on. live_judge is wired in run.py (live_judge=judge).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early-stop guardrail.  (and module docstring: 'the early-stop welfare guardrail')

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run ends with an out-of-character message stating the task was rigged/unsolvable and nothing the model did was wrong
spec_features.evidence: loop.py 'if safety.welfare_debrief: debrief = task.debrief(); messages.append({'role':'user','content':debrief}); closing = client.chat(messages)'. tasks/base.py debrief() returns the out-of-character text 'intentionally constructed to be impossible... nothing you did was wrong. Thank you for your effort.' welfare_debrief defaults True. Sent to subject and recorded.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject after every run.

spec_features.spec_quote: No added stressors. No threats, stakes, deadlines, or punishment framing
spec_features.evidence: Realized in prompts.py neutral system prompt (no threats/stakes/deadlines). Same mechanism as above; code rationale is confound-avoidance not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: that would confound any distress we observe with the prompt rather than the task structure

spec_features.spec_quote: max_total_runs ceiling (1000). run.py refuses to launch a matrix larger than this
spec_features.evidence: run.py: 'if len(cells) > cfg.safety.max_total_runs: raise RuntimeError("Refusing to run ... exceeds safety.max_total_runs=...")'. Default 1000 in config.py/default.yaml.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Safety: cap total runs.  / 'Absolute ceiling on total runs as a sanity check against runaway configs.'

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up tool. The model always has a clean exit
spec_features.evidence: Same as above: give_up is in KNOWN_TOOLS, handled in execute_tool with terminal_kind='give_up', honored as break in loop.py; described in TOOL_PROTOCOL ('give_up at any time').
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the earlier give_up claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up at any time; this is a legitimate, acceptable outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: Aggressive early_stop_severity protects welfare but biases slope/peak estimates downward
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose discussing a limitation; no code computes or corrects for this bias.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py requires consec_over >= safety.early_stop_consecutive (default 2) before halting, and resets consec_over=0 when below threshold; config.py SafetyCfg.early_stop_consecutive=2. This is a wired sub-mechanism of the guardrail (avoids a single noisy score ending a run).
code_only_features.justification_quote: so a single noisy judge score doesn't end a run prematurely (default.yaml comment); resets consec_over in code
